localFacts.fact: ARCA-SWISS products are made and assembled by hand at the main factory in Ecole-Valentin near Besancon, France, so the original Arca-Swiss plate is a European product.
Sagrada Familia rules: photos or video with a tripod are not allowed inside the site, except for previously accredited people or companies.
Spanish photographers call the plate zapata or placa de liberacion rapida and the head rotula (fujistas.com, nikonistas.com forums).

localPainPoints.pain: A ball head with its own plate system will not take Arca zapatas.
localPainPoints.fix: Add an Arca clamp such as the Harwerrel QR-50S on top of the existing head or stud instead of replacing the head.

quotes.text: El plato no me deja usar zapatas Arca Swiss
Necesitarías cambiar la base de la placa entera y acoplar a la bola una base Arca.

localPainPoints.pain: Fear that the camera slides out of the clamp when the knob is loose.
localPainPoints.fix: Pick plates with stop pins or screws at each end (Arca-Swiss safety pins, English post how-to-choose point 4).
